title: Cross Country Suite on Dot Records
summary: Riddle's eleven-part suite was recorded for Dot, won a Grammy, and was recently reissued.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: at the time, liked the idea and he brought the idea to the attention of Dot Records and convinced them to do this LP and we made an LP and Nelson called it Cross Country Suite. And it still holds up great. When you hear it, it still sounds good. And it’s one of the real combinations of jazz and symphonic approach without being too mechanical or too obvious. It’s a really good musical experience that comprised the jazz feeling and the orchestral approach, the symphonic approach. In fact, it won an award at that time for Nelson. One of the first Grammy awards, for Nelson. Yeah. It was recently re-released by Nelson’s daughter.
It’s amazing; she put out a CD, had it re-mixed.
I’m trying to think of her name, Sarah.
And it turned out really nice.
A lot of people now are probably hearing it for the first time.
Yeah. And it sounds valid, it sounds good. It’s one of the better compositions of the past twenty-five, thirty, forty, fifty years. [laughter]
Nelson was just a marvelous person, great, and very warm. Had great humor.
And his writing of course. You know.
His writing is exceptional, unexcelled. It’s not only Cross Country Suite, everything he wrote, most everything he wrote for the . . .
